  Promote a safe work environment paying particular attention to food and drink safety

  Complimentary coffee, tea, hot chocolate and soda while on shift, when using your reusable cup
  30% discount off regular-priced merchandise at The Trading Post Gift Store
  30% discount at Stanley's Bar & Grill and Prospect Point Café
  Free staff meal while on shift
  30% discount on food & beverage items in The Cliff House Restaurant, Loggers' Grill, Beary Waffles, and The Cabin at Capilano Suspension Bridge Park(does not apply to alcohol)
  Guest passes for friends & family
  Referral bonuses
  Employment & Family Assistance Program, offering five free online counselling sessions per topic for our staff
  Job Qualifications & Considerations
 
  Previous food service industry experience
  Must have current Serving It Right certificate
  Must be able to work in a fast-paced environment with the ability to multi-task
  Positive attitude and a strong desire to provide experiences Guests are amazed by
  Strong communication skills, multilingual is considered an asset
  Able to work a variety of shifts including evenings, weekends and holidays, to meet the needs of the business
  Occasionally required to lift and carry up to 20lbs, climb a step ladder or climb a step stool
  The wage for this role is $18.21 per hour plus gratuities. This role is a seasonal summer contract that will run from May through to September 2026.
  The Capilano Group comprises of retail, hospitality and tourism-based businesses anchored by Capilano Suspension Bridge Park in North Vancouver. The Capilano Group’s portfolio includes Moraine Lake Lodge, Moraine Lake Trading and Cathedral Mountain Lodge in the Canadian Rockies, Stanley Park Pavilion, Stanley’s Park Bar & Grill and Prospect Point Café and Gift Shop in Stanley Park, Vancouver and Capilano Suspension Bridge Park, Capilano Trading Post in North Vancouver.

title: Barista - job post
description:
WHO WE ARE
We are a specialty micro bakery and cafe located in the heart of Kits committed to providing our customers with freshly made, health oriented baked goods made with the highest quality ingredients. We believe that everyone deserves to experience having delicious baked goods in a wonderful setting along side the best tasting coffee this side of town.
JOB DESCRIPTION
Latte art skills and the ability to steam perfect micro-foam is a must. We are looking for enthusiastic front-of-house baristas to join our team. The position requires relevant experience working on an espresso machine, including being able to expertly steam milk to create micro-foam and latte art. As a barista, you will be working in a small space alongside other baristas, bakers and front-of-house staff. It is important that you are able to maintain excellent levels of quality and cleanliness. Cleaning is a big part of this job and when there are no customers to serve, it will be necessary to perform other tasks such as wash and put away dishes, wipe down appliances, tidy the coffee station area, clear tables, sweep and mop floors and always maintain a clean environment. This position includes closing shifts as well, which takes 2-3 hours. You must be okay with cleaning being a large part of your responsibilities.
QUALIFICATIONS

 At least 1 year of proven experience serving espresso based drinks.
 Ability to serve multiple coffee and tea orders at the same time while maintaining the highest quality standards is required.
 Attention to detail and the ability to stay focused while maintaining a positive attitude in a high-paced, busy environment is a must.
 Ability to follow instructions and maintain a high level of professionalism while providing top customer service.
 An outgoing, friendly and respectful attitude towards customers and other staff is required.
 Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, fluent in English or native speaker.
 A passion for coffee is a plus.

What you'll work on:

 Welcome customers walking in, take orders and operate a point of sale
 Serve baked goods and breads to customers
 Prepare coffee on an espresso machine: pour shots and froth milk carefully
 Prepare tea and tea lattes
 Explain beverages and food items to customers
 Quality control of espresso and grinder throughout the day
 Prepare sandwiches and other quick prepared food tasks
 Clean espresso machine at the end of the day
 Empty and replace bus bins
 Stamp bags and refill tea, coffee and any items necessary
 Accept and store deliveries
 Refill pastry cases carefully and keep them clean
 Wash and put away any dishes as needed throughout the day
 Maintain a clean and tidy workspace, washing hands frequently
 Monitor inventory and supply levels
 Note items that are low in stock
 Ability to lift up to 20kg
 Sweep and mop floors
 Clean sinks, countertops, glass displays and appliances (fridges, ovens, etc)
 Clean bathroom, windows and other cleaning tasks
 Sort and take out recycling, take out garbage and compost
 Deep cleaning shifts may be scheduled on occasion

CONTACT INFO
Interested applicants please submit your resume alongside references. Cover letter not required but appreciated.
Only qualified applicants will be considered and contacted for interviews.
DETAILS
Current shift offering is around 30 hours per week including weekends (must be available both Saturday and Sunday to work both days). Some shifts will be closing.
Base wage is from $18.50 with pooled gratuities that usually range between $2-3 per hour. Wage is negotiable based on experience and barista skills.

Pay: $18.50-$20.50 per hour
Expected hours: 28 – 35 per week

title: Experienced Fine Dining Server - job post
location: 915 West Hastings Street, Vancouver, BC V6C 1C6
description:
WHO WE ARE
 The Vancouver Club is a distinguished private members club nestled in downtown Vancouver. Established in 1893, the Club has a rich history and a commitment to exceptional service offering an array of amenities, including dining, function spaces, accommodations, and fitness facilities. The Club is dedicated to providing unparalleled meaningful experiences for its members.
 OPPORTUNITY OVERVIEW
 We are looking for experienced server, preferably in fine dining, dedicated to exceeding expectations of both our members and guests to ensure the highest level of service is consistently provided. Teamwork is the key to success in providing a warm and personable experience, the role is to provide excellent guest service with the support of the Food & Beverage team. The Server will have a strong desire to learn and develop within the hospitality industry. The Club looks for career focused professionals that are excited to experience all this industry has to offer.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
 
  Provide friendly, knowledgeable service and build positive relationships with guests and colleagues.
 
 
  Understand and follow all service standards, Club policies, and procedures.
 
 
  Maintain cleanliness and readiness of assigned stations and work areas.
 
 
  Set up and break down stations and prepare for next service.
 
 
  Participate in team meetings and stay informed on events, menus, and promotions.
 
 
  Demonstrate full knowledge of food, beverage, dessert, wine, coffee, and tea menus.
 
 
  Confidently make menu suggestions and answer guest questions.
 
 
  Handle all payment procedures accurately.
 
 
  Follow health and safety procedures and all duties as assigned.
 
 
  Address guest concerns and provide feedback to management.
 
 
  Strive for excellence in service and attentiveness.
 
 
  Memorize menu features and be engaged during pre-shifts.
 
 
  Support guest satisfaction and review feedback with supervisors.
 
 
  Other duties as assigned.
 
 
 QUALIFICATIONS & SKILL REQUIREMENTS
 
  One to three years of service experience in a fine dining establishment
 
 
  Excellent written and verbal communication skills
 
 
  Demonstrate superior customer service philosophy
 
 
  Must have Serving it Right certification
 
 
  Must have FOODSAFE Level 1 certification
 
 
  Will be required to maintain a flexible work schedule
 
  Available Wednesdays-Fridays, shifts range from 3pm-11pm or 4pm-12am
 
 COMPENSATION
 Hourly wage $24-30 per hour. No Gratuities
 
 WHAT WE OFFER
 
  Daily staff meals
 
 
  RRSP contribution after 1 year of employment
 
 
  Extended health and dental benefits after three months
 
 
  Uniform and dry cleaning provided
 
 
  Staff events
 
 
  $25 off haircuts at the Club's salon

title: Materials Handler Coordinator - job post
description:
We are currently seeking a full-time Materials Handling Coordinator to join our Manufacturing team in Richmond, B.C. This role is critical to the safe, accurate, and efficient movement of materials throughout our facility. Acting as the primary shipping and receiving function on site, the Materials Handling Coordinator ensures raw materials, packaging, and finished goods are received, staged, shipped, and recorded accurately while supporting uninterrupted production flow.
  This position is ideal for a detail-oriented, safety-focused professional who thrives in a fast-paced manufacturing environment and enjoys collaborating across production, inventory, and distribution teams.
  
   What you will be doing:
   Material Handling & Production Support
  
   Safely coordinate the movement of raw materials, ingredients, and packaging in alignment with production schedules and work orders
   Stage, label, and prepare materials accurately to prevent errors, delays, or production downtime
   Maintain clean, organized, and food-safe material storage and staging areas
   Communicate material availability, shortages, quality concerns, and inventory discrepancies promptly to Production, Inventory Control, and Operations
   Support multiple production areas and adjust priorities as schedules and volumes change
  
   Shipping & Receiving
  
   Perform all shipping and receiving activities for the manufacturing facility with a strong safety-first approach
   Receive inbound materials and packaging, verifying quantities, condition, lot codes, and documentation accuracy
   Ship finished goods to the Burnaby Distribution Centre according to internal transfer requirements and timelines
   Prepare and maintain accurate shipping documentation, internal transfer records, and bills of lading
   Coordinate carrier pickups and internal transportation to ensure timely and accurate transfers
  
   Inventory Control & Accuracy
  
   Record all inventory movements in real time using RFID scan guns and ERP systems
   Maintain accurate inventory locations, lot tracking, and quantities
   Assist with cycle counts, physical inventories, and reconciliations
   Investigate inventory variances in collaboration with Inventory Control and Operations
  
   Food Safety, Quality & Regulatory Compliance
  
   Follow all food safety, quality, and regulatory requirements, including GMPs and HACCP
   Handle and store materials to prevent contamination, damage, cross-contact, or mix-ups
   Verify lot codes, production dates, expiry dates, and traceability information
   Support audits, inspections, corrective actions, and continuous improvement initiatives
  
   Systems, Documentation & Safety
  
   Maintain accurate and timely records in ERP and inventory management systems
   Follow SOPs, food safety programs, and site safety policies
   Safely operate forklifts, pallet jacks, and other material handling equipment
   Perform pre-operational inspections and report hazards, near misses, or unsafe conditions
   Promote a culture of safety, accountability, teamwork, and clear communication
  
  
   You'll bring:
  
   High school diploma or equivalent required
   1–3 years of experience in material handling, shipping/receiving, or inventory control (food or regulated manufacturing environment preferred)
   Strong commitment to workplace safety and food safety standards
   Experience with RFID scan guns, barcode scanners, and ERP or warehouse management systems
   Strong verbal and written communication skills
   Highly organized, detail-oriented, and adaptable
   Ability to work independently while remaining flexible to operational needs
  
   We Offer:
  
   A fun and supportive environment
   Vacation starting at 3 weeks per year.
   Group Health & Dental Benefits Program
   Participation in our Vacation Purchase Program
   One paid Volunteer Day each year
   Growth opportunities and a rewarding career with a Canadian business that takes pride in giving back to community
   Employee pricing on our product line-up
   And... a workplace filled with the aroma of coffee...all day...every day!
  
  Applications are welcomed from all individuals, including women, Indigenous people, persons with disabilities, visible minorities, people of all sexual orientations and gender identities, and others who may contribute to the further diversification of our company.
  Canadian Citizens and Permanent Residents will be given priority.
  To learn more about Canterbury, visit our website at https://www.canterburycoffee.com/.
  Monday to Friday, 6:30AM - 3:00PM Full-time, permanent, working 40 hours per week.

title: Food Service Worker, Patient Food Services, C&W - job post
description:
Food Service Worker, Patient Food Services, C&W
 
 Patient Food In-House
 Vancouver, BC
 In accordance with the Mission, Vision and Values, and strategic directions of Provincial Health Services Authority patient safety is a priority and a responsibility shared by everyone at PHSA. As such, the requirement to continuously improve quality and safety is inherent in all aspects of this position.
 The Food Service Worker performs various duties that include food preparation, cooking and assembly, and/or checking order accuracy for patients. The role follows established food recipes and production standards to ensure proper quality, serving temperatures and standard portion control, escalating to Cook, Supervisor, and/or Manager accordingly.
 What you’ll do
 
  Prepare patient meal items such as tea, coffee, toast, salads, sandwiches, milkshakes, infant formulas and tube feedings by weighing, measuring and combining ingredients.
  Assemble patient meal trays according to menu. Portions food for patients and/or retail food areas according to specified requirements.
  Load, deliver, collect, and unload meal service wagons.
  Clean soiled dishes and utensils; store cleaned dishes, trays and utensils in the appropriate areas.
  Prepare items such as vegetables and fruit by procedures such as washing, slicing, dicing and grating.
  Deliver food items from storage areas to work areas; rotate stock; remove food items from packaging, cans and/or freezer; label, package and transfer food items to freezer storage.
  Perform cleaning duties such as sweeping and damp mopping floors, cleaning counter tops, sinks, machines and equipment and spot washing walls and splash areas; remove garbage as required.
  Carry pans, kettles, and trays of food to and from workstations, stove and refrigerator in accordance with safety standards
  Store food in designated areas following wrapping, dating, food safety and rotation procedures.
  Notify leadership of retail product inventory when low.
  Perform other related duties as required.
 
 What you bring
 Qualifications
 
  Grade 10 plus one year’s recent related experience or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.
  Certificate in Food Safe Level 1
  Demonstrated knowledge of the historic and ongoing impacts of settler colonialism on Indigenous Peoples in social and health contexts, including supported by significant knowledge of Indigenous-specific mandates, including clear understanding of and commitment to eradicate Indigenous-specific racism and discrimination and embed Indigenous Cultural Safety and Humility.
  Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of the historic and ongoing impacts of settler colonialism and systemic racism on Indigenous Peoples within social and health contexts. This includes understanding how these factors contribute to current health disparities and barriers to care. Show a clear commitment to identifying, challenging, and eradicating Indigenous-specific racism and all forms of discrimination impacting equity-deserving groups within health care settings. This involves familiarity and understanding Indigenous Cultural Safety and Humility recognizing personal biases, institutional barriers, engaging in anti-racism education and training and advocating for systemic change.
  Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of legislative obligations and provincial commitments within Patient Food In-House contexts found in the foundational documents including Truth & Reconciliation Commission’s Calls to Action (2015), In Plain Sight (2020), BC's Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (2019), United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), Reclaiming Power and Place Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women & Girls Calls for Justice (2019), the Declaration Act Action Plan and Remembering Keegan: A First Nations Case Study - BC Human Rights Code, BC Anti-racism Act and how they intersect across the health care system.
 
 Core Competencies
 
  Brings an understanding of the Indigenous specific racism and the broader systemic racism that exists in the colonial health care structure, and has demonstrated initiatives in breaking down barriers and ensuring a safe environment ensuring a sense of belonging to all and informed by Indigenous Cultural Safety.
  Awareness of social, economic, political and historical realities of settler colonialism on Indigenous Peoples and familiarity with addressing Indigenous-specific anti-racism, anti-racism and Indigenous Cultural Safety and foundational documents and legislative commitments (the Declaration Act, the Declaration Action Plan, TRC, IPS, Remembering Keegan, etc.).
 
 Skills & Knowledge
 
  Ability to communicate effectively both verbally and in writing.
  Ability to deal with others effectively.
  Physical ability to carry out the duties of the position.
  Ability to organize work.
  Ability to operate related equipment.
  Demonstrates a commitment to beginning and/or continuing their personal learning journey related to Indigenous-specific racism and dismantling systems of oppression, as well as addressing racism more broadly. Shows willingness to articulate and share their learning experiences to contribute to a culture of motivation and inspiration among peers.
  Demonstrates foundational knowledge of the social, economic, and political realities of settler-colonialism and its impacts on Indigenous peoples and equity-deserving groups within social and health contexts. Understands the impact of social determinants of health-on-health outcomes. Shows a commitment to learning about and upholding legislative obligations and provincial commitments outlined in foundational documents such as the Truth & Reconciliation Commission’s Calls to Action (2015), In Plain Sight (2020), BC's Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (2019), United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), Reclaiming Power and Place: Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women & Girls Calls for Justice (2019), the Declaration Act Action Plan, Remembering Keegan: A First Nations Case Study, the BC Human Rights Code, Anti-Racism Data Act, and the Distinctions Based Approach.
 
 What we bring
 Every PHSA employee enables the best possible patient care for our patients and their families. Whether you are providing direct care, conducting research, or making it possible for others to do their work, you impact the lives of British Columbians today and in the future. That’s why we’re focused on your care too – offering health, wellness, development programs to support you – at work and at home.
 
  Join one of BC’s largest employers with province-wide programs, services and operations – offering vast opportunities for growth, development, and recognition programs that honour the commitment and contribution of all employees.
  Access to professional development opportunities through our in-house training programs, including +2,000 courses, such as our San’yas Indigenous Cultural Safety Training course, or Core Linx for Leadership roles.
  Enjoy a comprehensive benefits package, including municipal pension plan, and psychological health & safety programs and holistic wellness resources.
  Annual statutory holidays (13) with generous vacation entitlement and accruement.
  PHSA is a remote work friendly employer, welcoming flexible work options to support our people (eligibility may vary, depending on position).
  Access to WorkPerks, a premium discount program offering a wide range of local and national discounts on electronics, entertainment, dining, travel, wellness, apparel, and more
 
 Job Type: Regular, Full-Time Wage: $24.34 / Hour Location: 4500 Oak St, Vancouver, BC V6H 3N1 Closing Date: Until Filled Hours of Work: 0730 - 1530 / 1200 - 2000 (Tuesday to Saturday) Requisition #: 194723E
 
  What we do
 The Provincial Health Services Authority (PHSA) plans, manages and evaluates specialized health services with the BC health authorities to provide equitable and cost-effective health care for people throughout the province. Our values reflect our commitment to excellence and include: Respect people – Be compassionate – Dare to innovate – Create equity – Be courageous.

 PHSA is committed to anti-racism and equity in our hiring and employment practices. With learning and compassion, we are addressing existing inequities and barriers throughout our systems. PHSA is seeking to create a diverse workforce and to establish an inclusive and culturally safe environment. We invite applications and enquiries from all people, particularly those belonging to the historically, systemically, and/or persistently excluded groups identified under the B.C. Human Rights Code.

We welcome Indigenous individuals to apply and/or contact the Sanya’k̓ula Team (Indigenous Recruitment & Employee Experience) for support at indigenous.employment@phsa.ca.

These initiatives align with an Indigenous rights-based approach, recognizing the inherent rights and title of BC First Nations and self-determination of all First Nations, Inuit and Métis communities. PHSA is mandated to uphold legislative obligations and provincial commitments found in the foundational documents including the Truth & Reconciliation Commission’s Calls to Action (2015), In Plain Sight (2020), BC's Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (2019), United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), Reclaiming Power and Place Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women & Girls Calls for Justice (2019), the Declaration Act Action Plan and Remembering Keegan: A First Nations Case Study.

description:
PERMANENT PART-TIME

title: Restaurant Manager - job post
description:

 When joining Splitsville as a Restaurant Manager, you'll receive a comprehensive induction to set you up for success, with full training across all areas of our busy centre—including the lanes, bar and diner, and the amusements area.
 
  In this fast-paced and diverse environment, Restaurant Managers take the lead in delivering exceptional guest experiences while maintaining high standards of service and operational excellence. Drawing on your restaurant management experience, you’ll play a hands-on role both front and back of house—ensuring smooth day-to-day operations, inspiring your team, and supporting the wider leadership team in hitting key business goals.
 
 
 
  You will support the Centre Manager and team by helping drive performance across our four key areas: the lanes, the bar, the diner, and amusements—always with a sharp eye on guest satisfaction, team motivation, and commercial results.
 
 
 
  With your passion for quality service and team development, you’ll help create a welcoming, energetic environment where families make lasting memories, and team members are empowered to thrive and grow in their careers.
 
  To be successful you will have:
 
  Proven experience in restaurant management, ideally in a high-volume or semi-fine dining environment
  A strong passion for delivering exceptional guest service with attention to detail
  Demonstrated success in achieving financial targets and driving revenue growth
  A track record of leading, inspiring, and developing large, diverse teams
  Flexibility to work evenings, weekends, and peak trading periods
  A results-driven mindset with a clear ambition to grow and succeed
  A friendly, energetic, and professional approach with a can-do attitude
  A collaborative team player who thrives in a busy, hands-on environment
  Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, both front and back of house
  Skilled in organizing shifts, delegating tasks, and managing team performance
  Comfortable operating in fast-paced, guest-focused settings where no two days are the same
 
 The Who...
 Splitsville Entertainment is Canada’s premier family entertainment centre! Our modern facilities combine state-of-the-art 10 pin bowling, high-quality casual dining, arcades, laser tag, and other entertainment options to make your visit a one-of-a-kind experience.

Individual differences and the contributions of all employees are recognised and valued and we believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace makes us a more relevant, more competitive, and more resilient company.
 
   -
